title: Start deterministic Valve generator foundations without inventing Siemens contract facts
goal: Begin real GEN-VALVE-001 product development in parallel with #61 by implementing only generator capabilities that do not depend on the still-unqualified fbValve_Solenoid interface. Build deterministic output identity/manifest, safe output containment, Siemens-side engineering-name and symbol validation/allocation, and stable input diagnostics now; defer exact Valve call parameters, dependency names, versions and instance/data ownership until #61 produces the verified V21 contract.

baselineEvidence.firstRunOutcome: Pre-publication deterministic Linux acceptance failed after a partial OpenRouter workspace; no candidate PR was published and repair budget was not consumed.
baselineEvidence.contextLesson: The first run also placed Siemens-specific naming policy in Domain and sorted fields while computing canonical identity. Both are rejected by this refined authority: Domain/PlcCompiler remain vendor-neutral and semantically meaningful parsed-model ordering is preserved.

scope: Work only in Domain, PlcCompiler/IR, SiemensBackend, GeneratorCli, focused tests and examples listed in candidatePolicy.allowedPaths. Do not modify TiaV21Worker, workflows, agents, tasks, runner configuration, vendor payloads, or IndustrialMDE.

Preserve the architecture boundary: Domain and PlcCompiler remain vendor-neutral and must not contain Siemens-named validators, Siemens engineering-name rules, profile/library types, filesystem/output-root policy, manifest/hash plumbing or vendor-specific diagnostics. Siemens-specific engineering-name/symbol validation belongs in SiemensBackend; GeneratorCli may orchestrate validation/output/manifest concerns without pushing them into Domain/IR.

Add deterministic multi-artifact output manifest plumbing suitable for the upcoming Valve slice. The manifest must contain generator identity, deterministic input identity, an explicit externally supplied opaque profile/contract identity token, and relative paths plus SHA-256 hashes for every generated PLC/source artifact. The manifest itself is not included in its own hash list; its bytes must nevertheless be deterministic. Do not fabricate a Valve profile identity or Siemens library metadata.

Derive input identity from a canonical representation of the normalized parsed input model, not from raw JSON whitespace, input filename/path, output path, timestamps, locale, machine identity or other environment data. Canonicalization removes representation noise only; it must preserve semantically meaningful list/order information from the parsed model. In particular, do not sort AutomationDevice.Fields merely to stabilize hashing because field declaration order affects emitted PLC/UDT semantics. Two inputs that parse to the same ordered model must have the same identity; reordered fields must not be declared equivalent unless the domain model explicitly defines that collection as unordered.

Enforce output-root containment for every generated artifact and for the manifest before write. Reject absolute paths, parent traversal and containment escapes using path-aware checks; do not use substring-only '..' detection as the security boundary, and do not normalize an escaping path into a permitted write.

Introduce the smallest centralized Siemens engineering-name/symbol policy in SiemensBackend needed for first-device generation: reject null/empty required names, invalid names that cannot be emitted safely, and case-insensitive duplicate allocated symbols. Do not silently rename user input unless an existing documented deterministic naming rule already requires it. Do not claim a broader Siemens identifier grammar than this task can test/support; keep the policy bounded to names emitted by the current generator.

Add stable diagnostic codes/categories and locations for malformed or omitted required type tokens, unsupported enum tokens, null/empty required data, invalid Siemens-emitted names, duplicate symbols and output containment violations. Keep generic parse/validation diagnostics vendor-neutral; Siemens-specific diagnostics stay at the SiemensBackend boundary.

Keep existing Motor UDT generation and the existing two-argument CLI invocation compatible. Any profile identity/manifest capability must be strictly additive; the current `GeneratorCli <input.json> <output-directory>` path must continue to produce `UDT_Motor.scl` for the existing example/regression without requiring a Valve profile token.

Do not convert the repository into a generic graph compiler, plugin framework, catalog abstraction, general SCL AST, new service layer or UI platform. Prefer a few focused value/policy helpers over a new framework.

Do not add any fbValve_Solenoid call, parameter name, dependency identity, version, DB requirement, multi-instance requirement, target-memory requirement or other Siemens fact that has not been proven by #61. The follow-up GEN-VALVE-001 completion step will bind these foundations to the verified contract.

requirements: Candidate changes are limited exactly to candidatePolicy.allowedPaths; Siemens.Engineering remains absent from Domain/PlcCompiler and no Siemens-specific engineering-name/profile/manifest/filesystem policy is introduced into Domain/PlcCompiler.

Same normalized parsed input with the same ordered fields plus the same explicit profile identity produces the same input identity and byte-identical generated artifacts and manifest across repeated Linux runs, even when non-semantic JSON whitespace differs.

A test proves canonical identity preserves model semantics: whitespace/property-format noise that parses to the same ordered AutomationDevice does not change identity, while reordering fields changes identity/output ordering rather than being silently normalized away.

The deterministic manifest contains generator identity, canonical parsed-model input identity, explicit opaque profile identity and SHA-256 for every generated PLC/source artifact. It lists only relative artifact paths, does not hash/include itself in its artifact hash list, and contains no timestamps, absolute input/output paths, locale, machine/user identity or other environment-specific data.
The manifest itself is emitted deterministically beneath the requested output root and repeated generation produces byte-identical manifest bytes.

Every output path is proven contained beneath the requested output root before write using path-aware containment. Absolute paths, parent traversal and containment escapes fail with a stable diagnostic and do not write outside the root.

Null/empty required names, invalid Siemens-emitted engineering names and case-insensitive duplicate allocated symbols fail with stable diagnostic codes/categories and locations rather than producing ambiguous SCL; Siemens-specific name policy implementation is in SiemensBackend rather than Domain/PlcCompiler.
Malformed or omitted required type tokens and unsupported enum tokens fail rather than silently defaulting semantics.

Focused Linux tests cover canonical input identity across whitespace-only representation differences and order-sensitive fields, deterministic manifest/artifact bytes and hashes, duplicate/invalid-name rejection, malformed/omitted type, unsupported enum and output containment including absolute/traversal escapes.
Existing two-argument GeneratorCli Motor invocation remains compatible and existing Motor UDT generation/current Linux regressions remain green.
No code, example or test asserts any unqualified fbValve_Solenoid parameter, dependency, version, ownership, DB or target prerequisite fact.
